thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO burn rate exceeded on /generate endpoint (3m window) - burn_rate=4.2, current_burn=18% :rotating_light:

alice (oncall): I see it. Paging now. I'll start triage.

raj (sre): I can help — looking at infra metrics and autoscaler. Any obvious spike in queue length or a model hotloop?

alice (oncall): queue depth up ~x3, tail lat p99 spiked to 820ms. No recent deploys in the last 4 hours.

maria (observability): adding dashboard links: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/generate-endpoint-overview — watch the green line (prefix cache miss).

chen (customer-ops): flagging customers with live traffic above 1rps: AcmeCorp, OmniHealth. Not yet on live support.

raj (sre): autoscaler seems healthy, GPU utilization at 61% across the pool. I suspect small bursts accumulating due to prefix cache misses.

alice (oncall): running quick query to check KV cache hit ratio.

alice (oncall): ```
# prometheus
avg(rate(redwood_prefix_cache_hits_total[5m])) / avg(rate(redwood_prefix_cache_requests_total[5m]))
```

alice (oncall): cache hit ratio dropped from 0.83 to 0.41 during spike window.

maria (observability): running a span sample pull — a lot of requests are short but uncached. Could be tracing mismatched keys after a rollout?

raj (sre): rollback? No rollouts. Could be a change in traffic shape from a partner. Can we throttle low-priority traffic?

alice (oncall): We have paging criteria that send to oncall when multi-window burn exceeds 3x on 3m window. The customer impact is low latency increase but SLO burn creeping. I propose temporary mitigation: increase prefix cache TTL for generated prompts, and add a short-term routing rule to favor cached model variants.

taylor (prod-eng): We have a config flag to favor cached variants (route_preference=cached). I can flip in console, but want to ensure no downstream regression.

raj (sre): Do it. Also, decrease the SLO alert sensitivity while we mitigate to avoid duplicate pages — change 3m window threshold from 3x to 5x for the next 30m? We should be careful not to mask a real incident though.

alice (oncall): I'll make the alert change. Action: increase burn-rate threshold for the short window.

alice (oncall): ```
# alertmanager patch (temporary)
- name: slo-burnrate-alert
  expr: max_over_time(slo_burn_rate[3m]) > 5
  for: 1m
```

maria (observability): Also creating a temporary dashboard tile for "cache-hit % by customer" so customer-ops can watch impacted tenants.

chen (customer-ops): thanks, will notify AcmeCorp support channel to give a heads-up.

taylor (prod-eng): flipping route_preference=cached to true for generate-v2. Monitor impact.

alice (oncall): route flip done. Early signals: p99 down from 820ms to 290ms for the last 2 min, cache hit ratio back to 0.78.

incident-bot: NOTE: alert snoozed for 30m by alice (oncall) — reason: active mitigation in progress.

raj (sre): Good. For follow-up: we should adjust our multi-window burn policy to be less sensitive to short-lived cache churn. Current config uses 3m/30m/1h windows with equal weights. I propose weighting windows and requiring sustained burn in at least two windows before paging.

maria (observability): Proposed rule: page when (burn_3m > 4 AND burn_30m > 1.5) OR (burn_30m > 2.5). This avoids noise from microbursts but still catches sustained regressions.

alice (oncall): I like the two-window approach. For immediate follow-up, create a runbook note and a dashboard entry with the new rule and baseline examples.

taylor (prod-eng): We'll also add a signal for prefix-cache hit delta per customer so we can auto-throttle non-critical tenants when their delta > 20%.

chen (customer-ops): please include a small playbook to contact customers automatically when we flip routing for their traffic. We need consent for certain regulated tenants.

raj (sre): Owner assignments:
- raj -> draft alert rule changes and runbook (PR to infra/alerts)
- maria -> dashboard tiles + sample queries per customer
- taylor -> routing flag in console + safe rollback steps
- alice -> update oncall paging doc and set temporary thresholds back after 30m
- chen -> customer comm plan and consent list

alice (oncall): ETA for PRs?

raj (sre): I can open alert PR in the next 2 hours, will include test vectors.

maria (observability): dashboard changes done in 45m.

taylor (prod-eng): routing flag change has a canary path, will add canary for 15% of traffic and then scale if stable.

chen (customer-ops): contact list ready, will send templated update after we confirm stability.

alice (oncall): Great. Reverting temporary alert patch now to re-arm with adjusted criteria will be a separate PR. For the record: incident classified as "SLO burn due to prefix cache miss surge, mitigated by routing to cached model variants and TTL adjustment". No customer-facing outage; minor latency impact to some tenants.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED: SLO burn resolved, duration 01:55:57, pages: 1, mitigations: route_preference flip, TTL bump.

alice (oncall): Filing follow-up postmortem. Will include proposed multi-window alert logic, exact alert math, sample queries, and the list of tenants affected. Assigning follow-up meeting tomorrow 09:30 PT.

raj (sre): Add an item to evaluate whether prefix-cache priming during deployments could avoid future spikes.

maria (observability): Also recommend adding simulated load tests that exercise cache cold starts and measure SLO burn behavior.

taylor (prod-eng): I'll add a small e2e test to the nightly that primes the cache for commonly used prompts.

chen (customer-ops): I'll draft the customer note and include opt-in/out for routing changes for regulated tenants.

alice (oncall): Thanks everyone. Closing thread. :white_check_mark:
